title: A home for your garden, wherever you play
author: Waldas Gamer Studios

sections.heading: Garden fixes
items: Both players begin with no tool equipped.
Turned the arrival rabbit to face its direction of travel.

sections.heading: Accounts and cloud-save integration
items: Added an Account & Cloud screen with email registration, sign-in, password-reset requests and sign-out.
Added explicit local/cloud garden selection, automatic syncing after local saves, revision-conflict protection and local backups before cloud downloads. Offline play remains available.
Added a private Your Valley website dashboard showing uploaded coins, animal population, XP, land coverage and wildlife visit/residency dates.

Supabase database setup is installed and signed-out access is denied. Redirect URLs are configured; public account launch still needs email delivery, live authenticated acceptance checks and manual publication.

intro: The rabbit has stopped attempting a moonwalk, and your spirit now arrives without immediately brandishing a hoe. Meanwhile, the valley is getting cloud saves. These clouds have considerably better filing cabinets than the ones Arthur complains about.
why: Starting with empty hands gives the first arrival room to breathe. The rabbit correction makes its little crossing read as an actual journey rather than a disagreement with physics.

The new account screen and private Valley Club dashboard let one garden follow its owner across devices. Coins, wildlife and progress belong together; nobody should need a spreadsheet to remember which hedgehog moved in.
Choosing a local or cloud garden is deliberate, and older uploads cannot silently overwrite newer ones. A backup stays on the computer before a cloud download replaces its local save.
issues: The development integration is ready for account testing, but the website and game have not been published. Redirect URLs are configured; a working confirmation and recovery email sender is still required before public registration.
Live checks confirmed that signed-out access is denied. Game save/restore and mocked account/dashboard tests passed; two-account authenticated database and real email delivery tests remain pending.
Sign-in is session-only for now. The dashboard shows the last uploaded snapshot, and cloud conflicts pause syncing until the player chooses how to resolve them.

title: Familiar faces at the garden gate
author: Waldas Gamer Studios

sections.heading: Arrival scenery
items: Replaced the crossing placeholder with the supplied rabbit, the flying placeholder with the animated robin, and the distant animals with the supplied bull model.
Added a textured rock outside each garden corner, with varied rotations that stay consistent when reloading.
Arthur now waits beside the northern entrance for your first arrival and returns to wandering after his welcome.
Reduced the rock’s game mesh detail while preserving its original source model and texture.

sections.heading: Studio notes
items: Updated the latest blog post with the previous Blender robin animation work and a dated development follow-up covering these arrival improvements.

intro: The temporary rabbit has handed in its notice. A proper rabbit has taken the role, the robin has brought its newly animated wings, and the bulls have agreed to stand in the distance looking as though they own the place. Arthur, meanwhile, has finally checked the arrival time.
why: The first arrival established the route and camera timing. Replacing its stand-ins with the supplied models makes those little look-around moments belong to the valley. The flying robin reuses the Blender animation made from the two motion references.

Four rocks give the garden corners a little visual definition without bringing back the perimeter wall. Their varied angles are repeatable, so loading a saved garden does not cause a geological reshuffle.
Arthur now waits beside the northern entrance until his welcome finishes. Being greeted is rather more welcoming when the greeter has not wandered off halfway through your approach.
issues: The rabbit and bull sources contain rigs but no animation clips. The rabbit currently uses a simple whole-body hop; the bulls have subtle breathing movement. Their full skeletal gait animations are still future work.
These arrival animals are scenery, not purchased livestock or new visitor discoveries. The robin’s separate wildlife visit still needs 1% water.
A missing texture connection on the rock was corrected during import. The original source models and textures remain intact.

title: Taking the scenic route
author: Waldas Gamer Studios

sections.heading: A walk into the valley
items: Added a gravel pathway following the northern mountains and hills down to the garden edge, using the supplied gravel textures.
New gardens now begin with a short downhill camera walk, gentle footstep bobbing and smooth looks toward a crossing creature, passing bird, birch tree and two distant animals.
The arrival leads into Arthur’s welcome. Escape, B / Circle or Start skips the walk; existing gardens receive the path without replaying the arrival.
Time, weather and ambience continue throughout the shared arrival, with normal single-player or split-screen play restored afterwards. The scenery placeholders do not count as wildlife visits.

sections.heading: Previous follow-up: the robin learns its moves
items: Created an editable Blender rig and reference-inspired idle, hopping and flight animations, preserving the source FBX and texture.
Connected the clips to garden movement and short low flights, while retaining the 1% water visit requirement and existing saved discoveries.

sections.heading: In development — 2 October 2026 (not yet released)
items: Replaced the crossing placeholder with the supplied rabbit, the flying placeholder with the animated robin, and the distant animals with the supplied bull model.
Added a textured rock outside each garden corner, with varied rotations that stay consistent when reloading.
Arthur now waits beside the northern entrance for your first arrival and returns to wandering after his welcome.

intro: The scenic route now has a little more to say. Here is the original arrival story, the robin animation work that followed, and a development follow-up from 2 October. The latest scenery changes are still waiting for their next release.
why: A new garden should feel like somewhere you have travelled to. The gravel approach connects the northern mountain scenery to the plot, while a short walk gives the valley a chance to introduce itself before Arthur does.

The camera follows the actual hillside surface, with a small walking bob and eased turns. Four staged moments give the journey a little life: something crosses your path, a bird passes, a birch catches your eye, and two animals stand further away.

Early captures showed grass growing through the new gravel. Admirable botanical enthusiasm, but rather poor path maintenance. We cleared the route and moved nearby tree placements back so the approach reads more clearly.

The robin follow-up gave the previously unrigged bird an 11-bone Blender rig with idle, hopping and flight clips, inspired by the supplied motion videos. Its wings can now do the work instead of relying on a whole-model bounce. No tiny pilot licence was required.

Development follow-up, 2 October 2026: the real rabbit, animated robin and bulls replace the arrival stand-ins; varied corner rocks define the plot, and Arthur waits at the entrance. These latest scene changes are not yet released.
issues: The original arrival used deliberately simple stand-ins. The development follow-up replaces their appearances, while keeping them separate from collectible or resident wildlife.
The first robin skin-weight pass pulled some head vertices with a wing. Those weights were corrected before export. The motion is authored from reference, not automatically captured from the videos.
The rabbit and bull files have rigs but no clips: the crossing rabbit currently hops as a whole model and the bulls use gentle breathing motion. Full skeletal gait work is still pending.

The upper mountain route remains scenery. Arrival completion, skipping, Arthur’s waiting state, corner placement and split-screen handover have automated coverage; physical controller testing remains outstanding.

intro: Previously, arriving in the garden involved the traditional Welsh practice of appearing out of thin air. We have now installed a path. The rabbit-shaped object using it has declined to pay council tax.
why: A new garden should feel like somewhere you have travelled to. The gravel approach connects the northern mountain scenery to the plot, while a short walk gives the valley a chance to introduce itself before Arthur does.

The camera follows the actual hillside surface, with a small walking bob and eased turns. Four staged moments give the journey a little life: something crosses your path, a bird passes, a birch catches your eye, and two animals stand further away.

Early captures showed grass growing through the new gravel. Admirable botanical enthusiasm, but rather poor path maintenance. We cleared the route and moved nearby tree placements back so the approach reads more clearly.
issues: The creatures and bird are deliberately simple placeholders. Their motion is staged for the arrival; they are not new collectible animals, residents or Field Guide discoveries. The birch uses the existing tree model.
The walk follows the lower approach. The upper mountain path is background scenery, and normal player movement remains inside the garden boundary.
Automated checks cover completion, skipping, existing-garden loading, continued clock updates and split-screen restoration. Physical controller testing is still needed.

title: A little breathing room
author: Waldas Gamer Studios

sections.heading: Menus and button hints
items: Restored the clean woodland-green garden pause and village shop menus, removing the decorative petal borders.
Button hints now float beside the analogue clock, with outlined text for contrast against the scenery. The daffodil tool wheel and its controller controls stay in place.

sections.heading: Notes from the studio
items: Added a website blog by Waldas Gamer Studios, with release stories, reasons for changes, recorded issues and development screenshots.
Manual publishing now creates one blog post per new release and includes it in the website update.

intro: The menus had dressed for a flower show. Lovely ambition; rather a lot of elbows at the tea table. We have asked the decorative borders to take the afternoon off and given the valley a little breathing room.
why: The decorative frames made the pause and shop menus feel busier than intended. Following player feedback, those panels return to their simpler woodland-green appearance. The daffodil tool wheel keeps its petals because they are the actual selections, rather than extra decoration.
Button hints now sit directly over the scene. A dark text outline helps them stay readable against bright skies and pale ground, without putting another box between you and the garden.

The changelog tells you what changed. This blog adds the why, the rough edges, and screenshots where we have them. Each manual release now preserves its own studio note, so the story will not quietly turn into next week’s story.
issues: Controller icons follow the device name reported by the driver. A PlayStation controller presented as a virtual Xbox pad will still show Xbox symbols. Hardware-specific behaviour needs checking on real controllers; the automated checks simulate input.
The new menu treatment follows feedback on the last update. Sometimes the most productive gardening tool is an eraser. No saved-garden format changes are needed for this update.
